issues.legal_issue: Admission to a cooperative housing society requires compliance with the prescribed application, payment, declaration, and membership-selection formalities.
material_facts: The committee admitted 39 people and allotted plots to them, but 20 applications were undated, and the records did not establish that the required membership payments were made within the prescribed time.
Except for one person, the applicants did not satisfy the applicable membership requirements; the committee admitted 38 people with undue haste without considering people on the waiting list.
The society’s rules required a written application, approval by the managing committee, payment of the membership fee and qualifying shares, and the prescribed declaration.
issues.conclusion: The 38 people were not legally admitted as members, and the allotments in their favour could not be upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Rules 24 and 30 of the Delhi Co-operative Societies Rules, 1973, and bye-law 5 required compliance with the application, approval, payment, and declaration formalities; those formalities could not be disregarded. Rule 25 also prescribed eligibility conditions. Clause 7 of the Lieutenant Governor’s award required the society to act in accordance with the award, including consideration of the waiting list. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: society_membership_dispute and (membership_applications_undated_or_missing or required_membership_payments_unproved or required_membership_declarations_missing or waiting_list_bypassed)

predicates.society_membership_dispute: The proceeding concerns the validity of admission to a cooperative housing society.
predicates.membership_applications_undated_or_missi: The society admitted applicants whose membership applications were missing or did not show when they were made.
predicates.required_membership_payments_unproved: The society’s records did not establish that admitted applicants made the required membership payments within the prescribed time.
predicates.required_membership_declarations_missing: The society admitted applicants without the declarations required for membership.
predicates.waiting_list_bypassed: The society admitted new applicants without considering people on its waiting list.

issues.definition: When a cooperative housing society dispute involves missing or undated applications, unproved required payments, missing required declarations, or bypassing the waiting list, the new admissions and related plot allotments are invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A managing committee cannot validly declare society members to be defaulters without authority and compliance with the applicable procedures and protections.
material_facts: The nominated committee declared members to be defaulters for non-payment and for not submitting affidavits.

The governing Act required a special majority of the general body and the Registrar’s approval for declarations of default, and the Court held that the nominated committee could not function after the relevant statutory transition.
The committee relied on a circular sent after the stated payment time had passed; it did not give members the required opportunity to show cause why their plot rights should be forfeited.
The Court’s award restricted the committee’s authority to declare members defaulters, and an interim court order remained in force for the petitioners in one of the proceedings.
The Court found that the declarations were connected with the effort to benefit new allottees.
issues.conclusion: The challenged declarations of default were illegal and unjustified, and the Chairman correctly restored the affected members’ membership where appropriate.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 92 and 32 of the Delhi Co-operative Societies Act, 1972, limited the nominated committee’s authority. A declaration of default required action by the general body with a special majority and the Registrar’s approval. The award and the society’s bye-laws also constrained the committee’s authority and required proper notice and an opportunity to respond. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: default_declaration_dispute and (committee_lacked_authority or required_approval_or_special_vote_absent or invalid_notice_used or members_denied_opportunity_to_respond or declarations_used_to_facilitate_preferential_admissions or court_protection_remained_in_force)

predicates.default_declaration_dispute: The proceeding challenges a cooperative society committee’s declarations that members were in default.
predicates.committee_lacked_authority: The committee making the declarations lacked authority to do so at the time.
predicates.required_approval_or_special_vote_absent: The declarations were made without the required general-body special majority or approval from the responsible supervisory authority.
predicates.invalid_notice_used: The committee relied on a notice that did not satisfy the society’s notice requirements or was sent after the stated payment deadline.
predicates.members_denied_opportunity_to_respond: The committee did not give members the required opportunity to explain why their rights should not be forfeited.
predicates.declarations_used_to_facilitate_preferen: The committee used declarations of default to make benefits available to other people through new admissions.
predicates.court_protection_remained_in_force: A court order protecting the affected members from default declarations remained in force when the declarations were made.

issues.definition: In a dispute over declarations of default, if the committee lacked authority, required approval or voting was absent, notice or an opportunity to respond was deficient, declarations were used to facilitate preferential admissions, or court protection remained in force, the declarations are invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Members declared in default for failing to submit further affidavits should be restored when they had genuine grounds for disputing the default and are required to submit fresh affidavits.
material_facts: Forty-two members had been declared defaulters for not submitting affidavits.
The members had submitted affidavits when they originally sought membership, but there was a dispute about whether they had submitted later amended affidavits.
Some members said that they had asked for the required form of amended affidavit but the committee had not provided it.
The Chairman found that 30 members had genuine grievances and accepted them as members on their submission of fresh affidavits.
issues.conclusion: The Chairman rightly accepted the 30 members as members on their submission of fresh affidavits.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the Chairman’s case-specific assessment of the members’ genuine grievances and his resolution of the affidavit dispute by requiring fresh affidavits. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this particular ruling.

rule.if: affidavit_default_dispute and members_filed_original_affidavits and (amended_affidavit_status_disputed or required_form_not_provided)

predicates.affidavit_default_dispute: The proceeding concerns members declared in default for not submitting affidavits.
predicates.members_filed_original_affidavits: The members had submitted affidavits when they originally applied for membership.
predicates.amended_affidavit_status_disputed: The members and the society disputed whether the members had submitted later amended affidavits.
predicates.required_form_not_provided: The members said they requested the form for a required amended affidavit but the society did not provide it.

issues.definition: When members declared in default for an affidavit-related failure had filed original affidavits and the amended-affidavit requirement was disputed or its form was not provided, they are restored on submission of fresh affidavits.

issues.legal_issue: Applicants whose funds the society retained without admitting or refunding them, and applicants entitled to membership following acquisition of their land, should be accepted as members when they satisfy the membership conditions.
material_facts: The society had retained deposits from four people for more than a decade without returning the money or admitting them to membership.
The society had agreed to offer membership to four other people whose land had been acquired, subject to their fulfilling the membership conditions; those people had applied.
issues.conclusion: The Chairman rightly held that the four depositors and the four applicants whose land had been acquired should be accepted as members.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the Chairman’s application of the society’s membership arrangements to the retained deposits and to the agreement to offer membership to people whose land had been acquired, subject to the membership conditions. No earlier cases were relied on for this ruling.

predicates.society_membership_dispute: The proceeding concerns entitlement to membership in a cooperative housing society.
predicates.society_retained_applicant_funds_without: The society retained applicants’ funds without admitting them or returning the funds.
predicates.land_acquisition_triggered_membership_of: The society had agreed to offer membership to people whose land was acquired, and those people applied for membership.

issues.definition: In a membership dispute, applicants in either of these circumstances are accepted as members if they satisfy the applicable membership conditions.

issues.legal_issue: Plot allotments should follow a fair priority order based on the members’ prior allotments, communications, payments, and relative claims.
material_facts: Some members had received specific plot allotments and communications about them at an earlier stage and had paid substantially more than other members.
Other members had paid less and had received no specific plot allotment.
The Chairman assigned priority classes based on those circumstances, and the Court found that priority order just.
issues.conclusion: The Chairman’s priority order for plot allotments was just and was to be given effect, subject to plot availability and the Court’s directions.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the Chairman’s assessment of priority based on the members’ prior specific allotments, communications, payments, and relative claims, and directed that allotments follow the priority order in his report. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.plot_allocation_priority_dispute: The proceeding concerns the order of priority for allocating plots among society members.
predicates.some_members_had_earlier_specific_allotm: Some members had received specific plot allotments and communications about them before other members.
predicates.members_differed_in_payments_and_specifi: Members differed in the amounts they had paid and in whether they had received a specific plot allotment.

issues.definition: When a plot-allocation priority dispute involves earlier specific allotments and communications or differences in payments and allotment status, allotments follow the approved priority order.
